alex_runtime: ran a couple nsys traces against the INT8/FP8 branch, seeing recurring host-device memcpy spikes aligned with KV eviction windows. trace attached: gs://redwood-internal/trace/1849994321.ns
maya_perf: can you paste the nsys command you ran? curious about the trace filters
alex_runtime: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o /tmp/1849994321 --sample=none ./serve_bench --model=redwood-int8 --seq-len=1024 --batching=auto`
maya_perf: nice. quick skim of timeline: lots of small memcpyHtoD around kernel boundaries, and dequant kernels appear as separate ops (dequant + int8_gemm) instead of fused path. that explains the extra hostcopy time we see.
sam_ml: did we enable the new fused-dequant kernels in the build? iirc that's gated behind `USE_FUSED_DEQ=1`
joanne_infra: build shows fused disabled on the CI image for the branch (we left it off after the fp8 regression). we can flip it on a canary image to test.
alex_runtime: perf numbers: median latency up ~14% on tail for mixed batches when dequant is un-fused. seen here (from nsys summary):
```
GPU activities: 682.1 ms total
  kernels: 490.3 ms
  memcpy HtoD: 92.4 ms (spikes at t=~120ms, 260ms)
  memcpy DtoH: 18.6 ms
User CPU: 120 ms
```
maya_perf: perfetto flame matches — hostcopy spikes coincide with KV eviction events (we mark evict nvtx). looks like eviction kicks in during batching windows and forces device->host ops for CLR entries.
sam_ml: tradeoff: fused int8 kernels remove explicit dequant hostcopy but require extra GPU memory and change numerical path; FP8 fused path less mature.
joanne_infra: proposed experiments:
  1) run with `USE_FUSED_DEQ=1` on canary image, same nsys args + `--nvtx-annotations`
  2) tune batching heuristic to avoid evict during active short-latency windows: lower eviction aggressiveness and prefer `max_latency_ms=25` for small batches
  3) add KV warming (prefetch top-k keys) after model load to smooth eviction spikes
alex_runtime: I'll do 1 & 2 tomorrow. quick reproduce command i used for perfetto: `python perfetto_trace.py --pid $PID --out /tmp/1849994321.pb` and then loaded into perfetto web.
maya_perf: also try one trace with `--batching=strict` (no auto) to see microbatch boundaries. curious whether continuous batching resolves hostcopy overlap.
sre_bot: alert: latency spike detected 1849994300-1849994400, p95 > 500ms for route `/complete` :eyes:
sam_ml: accuracy note: on our eval set FP8 + fused deq had ~0.2% delta on perplexity; INT8 fused deq had ~0.6% change. check eval-run 1849989000 for details.
alex_runtime: quick log excerpt from the nsys event stream showing NVTX markers and memcpy occurrences:
```
[120.123s] NVTX: KV_EVICT_START
[120.127s] memcpy HtoD size=1.2MB
[120.130s] kernel int8_gemm
[120.132s] kernel dequant
[120.260s] NVTX: KV_EVICT_END
```
maya_perf: that ordering implies eviction inserted between the compute blocks; if we can shift eviction to happen in background stream below compute priority, kernel overlap could hide memcpy cost.
joanne_infra: we can schedule eviction on stream 2 (low-priority) and pin prefetch to stream 3. need to vet CUDA stream semantics with current runtime.
alex_runtime: next steps: (a) run fused build + nsys (b) tweak batching config and run perfetto (c) run a canary with eviction-on-low-priority-stream. i'll post results in this thread.
maya_perf: add a trace with `--trace-level=kv` (our internal flag) so we capture per-key ops and timestamps.
sam_ml: add eval run to confirm accuracy delta; include sample prompts so we can diff generation changes.
joanne_infra: i'll prepare canary image & flip `USE_FUSED_DEQ=1` behind feature flag `fused_deq_canary=true`. will share docker tag here.
alex_runtime: thanks. uploading nsys + perfetto zips to gs://redwood-internal/trace/1849994321.zip ; will follow up with fused build traces. :thumbsup:
